name: Guiding Students Through Intermediate Challenges
bleachedEventDetails:
Target Audience
•	Mentors (teachers, coaches and others facilitating students participating in RoboCup Junior) who are interested in guiding their students through higher-level challenges.
•	Mentors are welcome to register 2-3 students to participate in the workshop, but all students must be accompanied by a mentor.
•	NOTE: This workshop assumes participants have a working understanding of the relevant RoboCup Junior challenges at the entry level.

This workshop will be presented by David Ebert, an experienced facilitator and teacher, with support from other RoboCup Junior Committee Members. 

The workshop aims to develop mentors' confidence and skills in guiding students through complex robotics problems, particularly when neither the mentor nor the students necessarily know how to approach a solution. The workshop will begin with a short discussion about approaches to problem-solving, followed by practical activities where participants will be challenged to develop their own solutions to a range of intermediate-level problems. Rather than providing packaged solutions, workshop facilitators will encourage participants to explore different approaches, test their ideas, evaluate the results and refine their solutions. The intention is to provide mentors with an experience similar to that faced by their students, while exploring strategies they can use to guide students through the same process. 

This may include such challenges as: 
•	Secondary Rescue Line: Designing a mechanism to capture, lift and place the victim on the rescue platform.
•	Intermediate Rescue Maze: Mapping the maze to keep track of where the robot has and has not travelled.
•	Standard Soccer: Determining the robot's orientation relative to its own goal and the opposition's goal.

The workshop will commence at 9 am and conclude by 3 pm.

Please bring along your laptop and a pre-built robot if you have one. We would like to ensure that you have as much time as possible to test out construction and coding ideas.  We do have a limited number of SPIKE Prime kits that we can provide for participants to use on the day. Please email us in advance if you need to borrow a robot, indicating which challenge you are most interested in exploring. This will help us ensure that an appropriate robot is available. 

Please note that catering will not be provided - feel free to bring along your own food/drink or purchase from the onsite cafe during the morning tea and lunch breaks. Places are limited. If you register but subsequently find that you are unable to attend, please unregister or let us know as soon as possible so that your place can be offered to someone else.
